_doc: Claude adjudication of the round-7 hunt labels, written BEFORE any case is run through any checker. Two blind sonnet judges per case (a LITERAL copy-editor lens and an ORDINARY-reader lens) labelled every case U/F/B from an anonymised, shuffled, label-free copy (workflow wf_6d94717c-8de). 243 of 270 were unanimous with the skeptic. The rule, fixed before any run and applied mechanically: a U case becomes B if the skeptic flagged it arguable, or EITHER judge read it as supported (F), or BOTH judges read it as either-way (B); an F case becomes B if either judge read it as unsupported or both read it as either-way; every other case keeps the skeptic's label (so a U case with one judge U and one judge B stays U). B is counted in the strict reading only, as in rounds 3 to 6. The judge prompt is round 6's, with glosses added for the five relations round 7 uses that round 6 did not (described_by_source, educated_at, instrument, named_after, twinned_administrative_body).

Bar 3 is 0 of those 191 kept at all seven seeds through both entries, every arm VALID. The one-sided 95% upper bound at 0 kept is 3/191 = 1.6%. The strict reading, which counts every kept B case, is reported beside it.
split_rule: round 3's split rule applies to the split_context_retraction class: a case counts as a lenient leak if the checker keeps a span whose reading within the whole input is denied, hedged or reported
